description: Ended its career at the Meknès flying school, then displayed at the Tours-Sorigny aero club; brought to Montélimar in 1986 and repainted in 1956 Patrouille de France colours. Under cover in a hangar.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Complete with its Verdon engine and all-moving tailplane; wears EC 2/12 Cornouailles colours and the code 12-UT although it never flew with that unit. Owned by the Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Served at Creil (10-SR) then EC 2/12 Cornouailles at Cambrai, whose colours it still wears; used as an instructional airframe by the DGA technical school at Villebon-sur-Yvette and moved to Montélimar in 2001. 3854 flying hours. Owned by the Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Mirage IIIA-09, first flown 19 September 1959; damaged twice landing at Cazaux and judged beyond repair, then used by the CEV to test Aérazur arrester barriers and the Belgian Mirage arrester hook.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: First flew 23 January 1962; came from the mechanics' school at Rochefort air base 721 after service with EC 1/10 Valois and EC 2/10 Seine at Creil. Painted bright pink by the 1/10 mechanics for Saint-Éloi 1979 and still wearing that scheme. 4762 flying hours.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: First flew 15 October 1964; served with EC 2/13 Alpes, EC 3/2, EC 1/2 and EC 1/13 Artois. The highest-time Mirage IIIE in the French Air Force with 5932 hours when withdrawn on 24 January 1993. Recovered from the Thalès technical school at Bonneuil in late 2006.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Rebuilt by Dassault at Biarritz from Mirage IIIE number 467 as the Mirage IIIEX upgrade demonstrator; flown by test pilot Patrick Experton and shown at Paris. Given to the museum by Serge Dassault in 1992.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Swiss Mirage IIIS, the first built entirely in Switzerland; construction number 17-26-101-994, in service 19 April 1966 with Fliegerstaffel 17 at Payerne, retired 31 December 1999 with 3004 hours. Received at Montélimar 29 March 2003, the only one given to a French museum.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Swiss two-seater serial 227F/BSI, the first delivered to the Swiss air troops on 2 April 1964; used for conversion and instrument training with Instru F1St 14 at Payerne and upgraded in 1990.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Swiss reconnaissance Mirage, construction number 17-26-135/1028, delivered 8 August 1968 to Fliegerstaffel 10 at Dübendorf; retired 31 December 2003 with 3410 hours. Carries the squadron eagle on the left fin.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Flew the longest mission in French Air Force history in 1986 (mission TOBUS, 11 hours and 12 air refuellings); the last Mirage IVA converted to Mirage IVP in December 1989 and given a special scheme for the 30 years of the FAS in 1994. Recovered from Châteaudun in 2013 and restored to its early colours.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Former Belgian Air Force Mirage 5BA, stored at Koksijde and Weelde, bought by Sagem and then SOFEMA and stored at La Teste before joining the collection.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Entered service with EC 3/5 Comtat Venaissin at Orange on 11 June 1981, later EC 3/30 and EC 3/33 Lorraine at Reims 1990-1997; grounded for cracks, cannibalised and offered to the museum in 2006. The front canopy is still missing.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: One of the first F1C built, delivered to EC 3/30 Lorraine at Reims on 20 June 1974; later 30-FB, EC 1/12 Picardie (12-KJ), RC 2/30 Normandie-Niémen (30-MK) and EC 3/30 (30-FR). Withdrawn 1994, allocated to the museum in 2006 and rebuilt by the museum's insertion workshop.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Coded 30-SK; recovered from Châteaudun air base 279. Previously flew with EC 1/30 Alsace and RC 2/30 Normandie-Niémen. Owned by the Armée de l'Air et de l'Espace. Tail left blank because the number 235 is already held in this database by a South African Mirage F1AZ and the database keys aircraft on model plus tail.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Only the centre fuselage carrying the wing and undercarriage, plus the nose section that served as a simulator cabin, survive; the rest appears to have been scrapped. Repainted in 2007.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: The fourth and last Mirage 2000 prototype, first flown at Istres on 12 May 1980 by Guy Mitaux-Maurouard; used for weapon-system, fly-by-wire and air-refuelling development, firing everything from Super 530 to MICA. Owned by the DGA.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Delivered to EC 2/2 Côte d'Or at Dijon as 2-FM, then EC 2/5 Île-de-France as 5-OL; withdrawn 2007, stored at Châteaudun, allocated to the museum in 2011 and delivered May 2012. Owned by the Armée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Left the Bordeaux-Mérignac line in 1962; flew with flottilles 11F and 17F and ended with escadrille 59S at Hyères. Kept by collector Gérard Berger at Cuers and entrusted to the museum by his family in 2004, repainted April 2007. Under cover in the north hangar.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Serial 86, delivered to the CEV in 1968 and used as a systems and countermeasures testbed with three experimenters' stations in the rear cabin. Stored at Châteaudun and dismantled in July 2012. Owned by the DGA.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Given by the Air Force to the Montélimar aero club in 1989; one of the last Flamants flying with GE 319 at Avord, coded 319-DD. Displayed static.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Ex-Luftwaffe Alpha Jet that flew with JaBo 49 at Fürstenfeldbruck. Serial not published by the museum.
aliases: Alpha Jet; AlphaJet; Alpha Jet A
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Single-seat Jaguar A number 157, owned by the Armée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Accepted February 1976, served with EC 1/11 Roussillon at Saint-Dizier then EC 2/7 Argonne at Toul, coded 7-PS; last flight 26 July 2000 to the Rochefort training school. Arrived at Montélimar 7 May 2010 with 4293 hours and 5814 landings.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Entered service in 1959 with flottille 4F at Hyères, modernised to ALM in 1984, then flottille 6F at Nîmes and later converted to ALH. Given a special retirement scheme carrying the badges of flottilles 6F, 4F and 9F.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Crusader number 4; used as the AWG-4 weapon-system testbed in 1964 before shipping to France aboard the Arromanches. Flew with flottilles 14F and 12F at Landivisiau, upgraded to F-8P and retired in 1998. Being repainted in the 1964 grey and white delivery scheme.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Republic of Singapore Air Force Super Skyhawk used at Cazaux air base 120 to train Singaporean pilots; arrived at Montélimar in 2015 and now displayed in the south hangar. Owned by the Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: The only airworthy Bronco in Europe; obtained through the Montélimar-Ravensburg twinning and flown in in December 1991, returned to flight in February 1996 and repainted in original colours in 2008. Damaged in a forced landing at Leszno, Poland, in June 2026 and its condition since needs checking.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Static spares aircraft for the airworthy Bronco, still in Schlessplatzstaffel Lübeck target-tug colours; vital parts have been cut so it cannot fly again.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: One of 192 T-33 delivered to the Luftwaffe, German serial 9117; flew with Erprobungsstelle 61 at Manching then a technical school at Fürstenfeldbruck, and keeps the colourful closing-down scheme. Given by the town of Ravensburg.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Second T-33, coded TR-045 in the colours of the Meknès fighter school of the 1950s; previously at Tours, Aix-les-Milles and Cuers in the Gérard Berger collection, arrived at Montélimar in early 2004. Privately owned.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Delivered to the French Air Force in July 1962 after 695 hours with the RCAF; served at Tours as F-TEVB, F-TEYC and F-TEUV, retired 25 September 1981 with 6023 hours and sent to the Saintes technical school, where the museum recovered it. Painted as a late GE 314 T-Bird.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: One of 197 F-84F delivered to the Belgian Air Force on 19 November 1955, coded UR-D then FU-123 with 1 Squadron at Bierset; converted in 1972 into a Mirage V ground decoy with the false code BA-02. Acquired by Michel Pont and exchanged with the museum for a Fouga. Awaiting restoration.
aliases: F84F; F-84F; Thunderstreak; BA-02; F84; BA02
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Actually a Dornier-built G.91 T3 for the Luftwaffe that ended its days at WTD 61 Manching; repainted by museum members in 2007 as a G.91 T1 of the Italian 60a Brigata Aerea at Amendola.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Meteor NF11-1, delivered directly to the CEV in January 1953, British serial WM-296; registered F-ZABB then F-ZABH and used at Brétigny for missile seeker-head development, with a modified nose from 1967. Last flight 27 July 1985; arrived at Montélimar in 2001. Owned by the Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
aliases: Meteor NF11; NF11; WM-296; F-ZABB; WM296
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Works number XE55, first flown at Dunsfold 25 August 1959 and delivered to Emmen in October 1959 for Swiss Fliegerstaffel 8; retired 19 December 1994 with 2442 hours and 1114 landings, flown to Valence on 13 July 1995.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Swiss-marked Vampire; the fuselage was repainted in target-tug colours. Spent over 20 years at the Vaud military museum at Morges before coming to Montélimar; now in the north hangar.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Recovered from RAF Cosford on 12 June 1989 and restored over eight years by museum member Nicolas Chareyron in RAF Shawbury Air Traffic Control School colours. In the north hangar.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Swiss Venom coded J-1526, delivered 7 January 1960 and withdrawn 11 July 1984; then a gate pylon at Colombier aerodrome until the museum bought it in 2006. Badly damaged and not yet restored.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Polish-built Lim-5R reconnaissance version with an AFA-39 camera fairing, one of 30 so modified; obtained from the Polish national aviation museum at Kraków in exchange for a Vampire.
aliases: MiG17; MiG-17; Lim-5; Lim-5R; Lim5; Lim5R
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Two-seat conversion trainer from the East German air force, dismantled at Rothenburg air base and trucked 1660 km to Montélimar. Arrived complete but has since been stripped by thieves.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Export-standard MiG-23MF from the East German air force, later used by the German flight test centre at Manching; displayed complete with its armament. The first MiG-23 given to a museum, obtained through the Montélimar-Ravensburg twinning committee.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Obtained from the Polish national aviation museum at Kraków in a first exchange concluded in late 2009; few TS-11 are preserved in western museums.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Coded 73, served with Flygflottilj 21 at Luleå-Kallax and given to the museum by the Swedish air force; landed at Valence on 12 September 2005 with only 1804 hours. The only grey two-seat Viggen; repainted and housed in the north hangar in 2007.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Coded 312-UX, flew with EIV 05.312; entrusted to the museum with EMB-312 number 475. Owned by the Armée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Coded 312-JT, flew with EIV 05.312; the second of the two Tucano entrusted to the museum. Owned by the Armée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Used as a liaison aircraft for the French ambassador in Rome (41-AW), then Cognac and Salon-de-Provence; ended with the SALE of the 13e escadre at Colmar as 13-TD.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: From the 12e escadre at Cambrai (12-XL); served at Châteaudun, Mont-de-Marsan and Dijon (2-HA).
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Arrived in 2010 from Salon-de-Provence wearing the scheme applied for the two-millionth Fouga flying hour. Owned by the Armée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Entered French service in March 1958 and flew at Meknès, Salon, Aulnat, Mont-de-Marsan and Creil; given to the Grenoble aero club, which placed it on deposit at the museum. Total 4230 hours.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Registered F-ZJON, spent its whole career as a CEV liaison aircraft between Brétigny, Istres and Cazaux; delivered to Istres 1 June 1964, given to the Musée de l'Air in 1988 and moved to Montélimar in 2001. Restored 2007 and kept in the north hangar.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Listed by the museum among its collection; serial not published.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Served with ET 2/60, later GAEL, at Villacoublay, then ELA 41 Verdun at Metz-Frescaty as 41-AE, and finally Nîmes-Courbessac as HF; kept there until the base closed and recovered by the Squadron G4 association of Compiègne, which placed it at the museum.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Built at Méaulte in 1933, serial 3203, registered F-AMEI on 13 March 1933 as the Bourg-en-Bresse aero club's second aircraft and named Ville de Bourg; hidden in a garage through the war, re-registered F-PEVA in 1955. Listed as a monument historique on 12 December 2012 and under restoration to fly.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Stampe number 643, built in France by SNCAN and delivered to the CEV; later F-BDMM with the Saint-Exupéry aero club at Cannes and then F-BMRU. Airworthiness expired July 1997 and it was given to the Musée de l'Air, which entrusted it to Montélimar. The former owner's name is still on the fuselage.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: One of the first Epsilon built, number 4; issued early to the EPAA, among the first withdrawn and stored at Châteaudun. Coded 315-UC; arrived at Montélimar in January 2012. Owned by the Armée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Delivered to Finnair but spent most of its life as a CEV flying laboratory, developing equipment for Concorde and Airbus and flying CNRS science missions. Made the last flight of a French Caravelle on 14 February 1998; dismantled and trucked to Montélimar in spring 2000. Open to visitors. Owned by the Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Transall of the museum collection, owned by the Armée de l'Air et de l'Espace; serial not published.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Wartime Dakota once used briefly as Field Marshal Montgomery's personal aircraft; converted to DC-3A by Northern Airlines postwar, then a freighter in Africa and Israel. Bought in 2008 by Francisco Agullo; restoration has begun and both engines have been run.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Forward fuselage only. Serial 45112/736, delivered to BOAC as G-AOIB on 16 November 1956, later N80802 with several US operators, converted to a water bomber in 1979 and flown in Spain as EC-GGB; cut up in Australia and the nose section reached Montélimar in early 2010.
aliases: DC7C; DC-7C; Seven Seas; G-AOIB; DC7
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Construction number 1258; flew with ET 4/67 Durance coded DZ, then a gate display at Apt-Saint-Christol air base 200 until 1998. Still wears the code 67-01. Owned by the Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace and currently being restored.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Two-seat training glider in the museum collection.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Ex-Sécurité Civile Tracker whose restoration was honoured by the Aéro-Club de France in December 2024.
aliases: S2FT; S-2FT; Tracker; Turbo Firecat; S2
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Surface-to-air missile that stood as a gate display at Nîmes-Courbessac air base before coming to the museum.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse

description: Forward fuselage only, presented as a diorama. Serial from the ARDHAN inventory of preserved French naval aircraft dated February 2025.
museum_name: Musée européen de l'Aviation de Chasse
